what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS) in adults. It helps reduce the number of MS flare-ups (relapses) and slows down the worsening of disability. It does not cure MS, but it can help you feel better and have fewer attacks.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as a shot (injection) under your skin (subcutaneous injection). You can inject it into your stomach (abdomen), the back of your upper arm, or your thigh. Each time you inject, choose a different spot to avoid irritating the same area. Your doctor or nurse will show you how to give yourself the shot. You can use a prefilled pen (autoinjector) or a prefilled syringe. Always check the liquid before injecting — it should be clear and colorless. Do not use it if it looks cloudy, has particles in it, or has changed color.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 63 micrograms (mcg) injected under the skin on Day 1. Then you take 94 mcg on Day 15. After that, your regular maintenance dose is 125 mcg every 14 days (every 2 weeks). Your doctor will guide you through this step-up schedule to help reduce side effects when you first start the medicine.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — as long as your next scheduled dose is at least 7 days away. After the missed dose, restart your every-2-week schedule from that new date. Do not take two doses within 7 days of each other. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store this medicine in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep it in its original carton to protect it from light. Do not freeze it. If frozen, throw it away and get a new dose. If you cannot refrigerate it, you may store it at room temperature (up to 77°F / 25°C) for up to 30 days, but keep it away from heat and light. Once removed from the refrigerator, do not put it back. Keep out of reach of children. Dispose of used pens, syringes, and needles in an FDA-approved sharps container right away.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it may make side effects like liver problems worse. Do not drive or use heavy machinery if you feel confused or dizzy. Avoid people who are sick with infections, as this medicine can weaken your immune system slightly. Do not share your pen or syringe with anyone else. Talk to your doctor before getting any vaccines while on this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you have: signs of liver problems (yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, severe stomach pain, unusual tiredness); signs of serious allergic reaction (difficulty breathing, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, hives); signs of serious infection (high fever, chills, body aches); signs of depression or thoughts of harming yourself; sudden or severe chest pain or shortness of breath; blood in your urine or significant decrease in how much urine you make; severe injection site reactions such as open sores or skin breaking down. Also let your doctor know if you have worsening numbness, weakness, or MS symptoms.
when_it_works: This medicine works slowly over time. You may not feel a difference right away. Most people begin to see fewer MS relapses within 3 to 6 months, but it can take longer. It is important to keep taking it even if you feel fine, because it is working in the background to protect your brain and spinal cord. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The risks and benefits should be discussed with your doctor. Children: This medicine is approved only for adults and has not been studied in children under 18. Liver or kidney problems: Tell your doctor if you have liver or kidney disease, as your doctor may need to monitor you more closely. Depression: If you have a history of depression or mood problems, tell your doctor before starting this medicine, as it may make those conditions worse.
